description: Cool night, the mirror image. The bedroom is 78 F against a 72 F sleep ceiling while the hallway is satisfied. The loop LOWERS the cool setpoint by 2 F, the AC starts, the loop holds while it runs and steps the setpoint back up once the reading passes target - swing.

events.note: The hallway thermostat's own sensor: satisfied, so it will not start by itself.
Day classification (cold: heat all night / hot: cool all night).
Bedtime: the sleep band is written and the sleep window (remote sensor in use) begins.
The AC starts 3 s after the first step (72 -> 70).
Bedroom still warm: hold at 70, NO second step to 68.
Reading passes target - swing (72 - 1.5 = 70.5): step down (raise the cool setpoint).

assertions.reason: Entering the sleep window starts from no offset: the plain sleep ceiling, even though the bedroom is 6 F over it.
THE COMPENSATION (cool mirrors heat): the bedroom is warmer than target + swing, so the cool setpoint is LOWERED one 2 F step so the AC starts.
The AC started: hold at 70, no second step to 68 while it runs.
The reading passes target - swing (70.2 < 70.5): the cool setpoint steps back up to the plain 72.
In band afterwards: no more writes.

notes: Three-exercise protocol (CLAUDE.md section 10), Issue #1194 increment (e). Tier A: the real ClimateAdvisorCoordinator + AutomationEngine under FakeHass/FakeScheduler (use_coordinator=true, so the sleep-sensor listener and the 1-minute timer are real); every assertion is track=integration for that reason and is evaluated, not skipped.

(a) Effectiveness: scratch-copy mutation run of this scenario against the production code (worktree untouched). It FAILS when M01: the whole offset deleted (the write path adds 0 and the check is a no-op); M07: 'fired -> hold' deleted (a further raise while the equipment runs); M08: the step-down deleted. Passes unmutated.

(b) Docs <-> production alignment: docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md 'Remote-sensor outer loop on the thermostat setpoint (Issue #1194, increment a)': 'Heat and cool are mirror images'; the rule table with gap = remote - target. Matches production.

(c) Occupant outcome if this regressed: A person asleep in a bedroom 6 F over their sleep temperature lies awake hot with the AC never having run. COOL MODE SHIPS SIMULATION-TESTED ONLY: this scenario and the two cool caps are its evidence.

verdict.summary: Warm bedroom gets the AC: the setpoint is lowered one step, held while it runs, restored at target - swing.
verdict.observed_behavior: 72 F at entry, 70 F one minute later, 70 F while the AC runs, 72 F once the reading is under 70.5 F, then silence.
verdict.expected_behavior: Heat and cool are mirror images (the offset lowers the cool setpoint).
